>peak oil

Garbage.

The one thing Mike Rupert couldn't have been more wrong on.

How can you run out of something that can be mass produced?

Oil (see: Hydrogen and carbon) being a finite resource is one of the biggest scams perpetrated on humanity in the last 75 years.

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fischer%E2%80%93Tropsch_process
The Fischer-Tropsch process requires huge amounts of energy. Where are you going to get that from?

This isn't about some hypothetical in my head, I know people, former military, support divisions, who have confirmed shipments of "FT Oil" to them. So whatever problem you think there is in the energy required to create it? They figured it out, and they didn't tell you. :)

This is quite simple. You cannot gypsy the laws of thermodynamics. While the FT method does produce energy in the form of oil it requires MORE energy to make that oil.

The concept is Energy Returned On Energy Invested (EROEI). It is only feasible to use the FT method when you have a huge source of energy that is 'cheap', in your case it is probably natural gas. NG is really quite cheap in comparison to oil. NG is however also a finite resource.

The FT method is only viable at the moment because oil is worth more natural gas. Ultimately though, the FT process results in a net loss of energy making in a rather shitty choice of oil production. Furthermore, natural gas is finite making FT unsustainable.

Peak oil is not a 'theory', it is a geological fact.

Wondering if it's possible to incorporate the number of comments over a given period of time in determining where a post places in the "hot" timeline.

Often times there's great potential for discussion and interest in a given thread but the actual up vote count does not reflect the interest level. Especially if the subject is controversial.

This is a great way of undermining the tryany of the majority in voting habits.

Edit* I did a spellings
Incorporate comment activity levels in algorithm determining front page placement/ranking.

I agree with this, especially if voat is to be a site where discussion is valued higher than low effort content.

The only problem is that this sounds like it would be really freakin' hard to implement.
Yeah. Ive got no idea how that would be implemented. Algorithms and coding may as well be magic for the amount I understand them.

It would have to count each threads time since posted, the total comment count and a frequency interval based on the time chart.

So a short time posted with a high comment frequency = very hot thread, but a very long time posted with a high total, but low frequency is a formerly hot thread with a few pugilists having it out.

Then it would have to compare it to all other posts in the sub and the site, so I imagine it would be pretty difficult.

As you mentioned, theres a lot to track, but I do not see it as difficult. Time consuming to implement and very expensive to process all that information on high traffic site.

There are some tricks you can do in a database, like indexing posts counts and using triggers to update a table that tracks post intervals and things like that. Also you can keep caches that are updated by background services.

But its still pretty expensive, no matter what.
